sections.title: The Circumcision at Gilgal
observations: After crossing the Jordan River, the Israelites camped at Gilgal, where Joshua commanded the men to be circumcised. This act was significant as it represented the covenant between God and His people, a renewal of their identity as God's chosen ones.
The circumcision was a necessary step before they could partake in the Passover, emphasizing the importance of being spiritually prepared before entering into God's promises.

sections.title: The Passover Celebration
observations: The Israelites celebrated the Passover at Gilgal, marking their first observance in the Promised Land. This event was a reminder of God's deliverance from Egypt and His faithfulness to His covenant.
The timing of the Passover, right after their circumcision, highlights the importance of obedience and remembrance in the life of God's people.

sections.title: The Commander of the Lord's Army
observations: Joshua encounters a mysterious figure who identifies himself as the commander of the Lord's army. This encounter emphasizes the divine presence and leadership in the battles to come.
The commander's instruction to Joshua to remove his sandals signifies the holiness of the ground, reminding Joshua of God's sovereignty and the need for reverence.

importantVerses.commentary: At that time the Lord said to Joshua, 'Make flint knives and circumcise the Israelites again.' This verse highlights the importance of covenant renewal and obedience to God's commands.

The manna stopped the day after they ate this food from the land; there was no longer any manna for the Israelites, but that year they ate the produce of Canaan. This verse signifies a transition from dependence on God’s miraculous provision to enjoying the fruits of the Promised Land.

The commander of the Lord's army replied, 'Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy.' This verse emphasizes the holiness of God's presence and the need for reverence in His service.

questions: What does the act of circumcision signify for the Israelites in the context of their covenant with God?
How does the celebration of Passover at Gilgal connect the Israelites' past with their present and future?
What can we learn from Joshua's encounter with the commander of the Lord's army about God's presence in our battles?
